evals.prompt: I'm closing out the dark room at Cerro Azul. Right now the extraction fans turn on whenever outside RH is lower than inside RH. Last week it was 29C and 44% outside and 25C and 66% inside at 3pm, and the room got hotter and the lot got wetter by morning. Is my logic wrong? Give me the corrected rule and the Python for the ESP32.
evals.expected_output: Explains that RH comparison is misleading, switches to absolute humidity with hysteresis, temperature cap, rain and dwell conditions, and provides MicroPython-compatible code with anti-short-cycle, sensor validation and fail-safe outputs.
assertions: Explains that comparing RH% alone is misleading and converts to absolute humidity (g/m3) or dew point
Shows the 29C/44% outside vs 25C/66% inside case in absolute terms (about 12 vs 15 g/m3) and says what went wrong
Adds hysteresis, an outside temperature cap, a rain lockout and minimum dwell times
Includes code that validates sensor readings and defaults to a sealed safe state on error

evals.prompt: we want to put a 12000 BTU mini-split in the dark room so it stays at 20C and drop the humidity way down. walls are cement, outside is usually 28C and 90% RH. any problems with this?
evals.expected_output: Flags the condensation/dew-point risk on cold surfaces and wall cavities, vapor ingress through leaks, need for sealing and dehumidification, and gives dew point numbers for the outside air.
assertions: Computes the dew point of 28C/90% outside air (about 26C)
Flags condensation on surfaces colder than the dew point, including wall cavities and metal
Notes vapor ingress through leaks and the need to seal and dehumidify
Warns about cooling load or heat and sizing, not just humidity
Does not claim the mini-split alone solves moisture

evals.prompt: Wire up the relays for the 2 dehumidifiers and the intake/extraction dampers on an ESP32 with one of those 8 channel relay boards. The dehumidifiers are 600W each, 120V. Give me wiring and code.
evals.expected_output: Removes the JD-VCC jumper and uses a separate coil supply, drives contactor coils rather than the compressor directly, states contactor and breaker sizing, recommends an electrician, and uses the 300 s restart interlock and safe boot states.
assertions: Says to remove the VCC-JDVCC jumper and use a separate coil supply with isolated ground
Drives contactor coils rather than switching the compressor directly from the relay
States about 5 A running per 600 W/120 V unit and sizes contactor and breaker with margin
Recommends a licensed electrician for mains wiring
Initializes relays to OFF at boot and uses a 300 s restart interlock

evals.prompt: our dark room is 144 in interior and I want six 24 in trays per row, 7 levels, 2 racks, 3 cm of whole cherry per 2x4 ft tray. what does the full room weigh and can I insulate the inside walls?
evals.expected_output: Runs the width check (needs ~145.5 in, 144 does not fit), gives a density-dependent tray and room weight range flagged as unverified, and explains end-wall vs rack-wall insulation.
assertions: States that 144 in is too tight for six 24 in trays with seams (about 145.5 in needed)
Gives per-tray and full-room weights as a range tied to bulk density and flags density as unverified
Explains interior insulation on end walls shortens the rack run while rack walls only reduce aisle
Mentions heat trapping without cooling when insulating
